newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan says Indian military acts raise tension.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan says Indian military acts raise tension.

text.p: Pakistani Foreign Minister Gohar Ayub Khan accused India on Thursday of raising tensions, raising doubts about a planned second round of peace talks between the two rival neighbours.

At a news conference, he cited a recent alleged violation of Pakistani airspace, the deployment of medium-range ballistic missiles near the border and a border clash on Tuesday night in which a Pakistan army major was killed, and said he was unsure if Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral approved of them.

"Mixed signals are coming from New Delhi," Khan said in an apparent reference to New Delhi's desire to attend a planned second meeting in Islamabad between top Indian and Pakistani foreign ministry officials.
The two sides resumed talks in March following a three-year hiatus.

"We are not sure whether what is happening is with the concurrence or with the knowledge of the (Indian) prime minister or these things are happening by the armed forces, or whoever is there," Khan said.
But he said he thought if Gujral had prior knowledge of such plans, "probably he would not authorise something like that".
Khan would not say if the Indian actions would jeopardise the next round of talks that Islamabad wanted to be held on June 19-22.
But he said: "They have not helped the negotiations. They have unnecessarily tensions on the Pakistani side and apprehensions."
India has yet to agree to the dates of the meeting, and Khan said the final dates would be finalised by the foreign ministries of the two countries.
Khan ruled out cutting defence spending in the budget for fiscal 1997/98 (July/June) to be unveiled on Friday, saying: "For Pakistan, to cut the defence budget will be suicidal."
However, he said if India cut its defence budget, Pakistan could consider doing so in the same proportion.

Khan's statement came after seemingly conciliatory remarks by Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz in a televised speech on Wednesday night in which he said the two sides should try "other means" after 50 years of hostility between them.

India has denied Pakistan's charge of airspace violation on May 27 by an Indian jet, which set off shockwaves that shook buildings in Islamabad, and Gujral said on Wednesday the reports that India had deployed its Prithvi missiles on border with Pakistan were false.

"We have not deployed Prithvi in any part of India and more so on our borders," Gujral told reporters in the western Indian city of Pune after inducting the first batch of Russian-built Sukhoi-30 fighter aircraft into the Indian Air Force.

A Pakistan military statement said on Tuesday that a major with paramilitary Rangers in the eastern Sialkot sector was killed by Indian Border Security Force firing from the Indian-ruled part of the disputed Kashmir region.
It said the clash followed "unprovoked firing" by the Indian BSF on civilians building an embankment on the Pakistani side of what it called the working boundary with Indian-ruled Kashmir.
"Pakistan Rangers retaliated, inflicting casualties on the BSF," the statement said. "However, the number of Indian casualties could not be ascertained."
The two countries have fought three wars since independence in 1947, two of them over Kashmir, two-thirds of which is ruled by India and the rest by Pakistan.
